title: Inheritance
seo_title: Secondary 4 Biology: Inheritance Worksheets (O-Level 6093 with Answers)
standard_text: Define gene, allele, dominant, recessive, codominant, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype and phenotype; use genetic diagrams to predict the results of monohybrid crosses, including 3 : 1 and 1 : 1 ratios and test crosses; explain codominance and multiple alleles using the ABO blood groups; describe sex determination; distinguish between continuous and discontinuous variation; describe mutation, including sickle-cell anaemia and Down syndrome; describe natural and artificial selection (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Biology worksheets on inheritance: alleles, genotype, phenotype, monohybrid crosses, test crosses, blood groups, sex determination, variation, mutation and selection. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Genotype is the alleles; phenotype is what you see.
body_html:
How to think about it

Each parent passes one allele of each gene.

  • Dominant (T) shows whenever present; recessive (t) only in tt. TT and tt are homozygous; Tt is heterozygous.
  • Draw gametes, then a Punnett square. Tt × Tt: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, a 3 : 1 phenotype ratio.
  • A test cross with tt shows if a dominant-looking parent is TT (all dominant) or Tt (1 : 1).
  • ABO: Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant, i is recessive. Sex: XX female, XY male; the sperm decides.
Example

Tt × tt. Chance of tt?

gametes T, t and t

Tt, Tt, tt, tt

Answer: 50%

Example

Iᴬi × Iᴮi. Possible groups?

IᴬIᴮ, Iᴬi, Iᴮi, ii

Answer: AB, A, B or O

Common mistakes

  • Saying the dominant allele is the more common one.
  • Reading 3 : 1 as an exact result.
  • Calling Tt homozygous.
  • Saying height is discontinuous variation.

faq.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
faq.a: The genotype is the pair of alleles an organism has, such as Tt. The phenotype is the feature you can observe, such as being tall, which also depends on the environment.
Both alleles are expressed in a heterozygote. In the ABO blood groups, a person with Iᴬ and Iᴮ has blood group AB.

faq.q: How is the sex of a baby decided?
faq.a: All eggs carry an X chromosome. Half the sperm carry an X and half a Y. An egg fertilised by an X sperm gives a girl (XX); by a Y sperm gives a boy (XY).

items.q: What is meant by a recessive allele?
c: the alleles an organism has, such as Tt
having two identical alleles of a gene, such as TT or tt
an allele that is expressed only when no dominant allele is present
having two different alleles of a gene, such as Tt
items.e: A recessive allele: an allele that is expressed only when no dominant allele is present.

items.q: Which genotype gives blood group O?
items.e: Only two recessive alleles give group O.

items.q: What is meant by a test cross?
c: the observable features of an organism, such as tall
an allele that is expressed whenever it is present
crossing an organism of dominant phenotype with a homozygous recessive to find its genotype
one of two or more forms of a gene
items.e: A test cross: crossing an organism of dominant phenotype with a homozygous recessive to find its genotype.

items.q: Which term means having two different alleles of a gene, such as Tt?
items.e: Heterozygous: having two different alleles of a gene, such as Tt.

items.q: Why is the observed ratio of offspring often not exactly 3 : 1?
c: Fertilisation is random, so small numbers of offspring do not match the expected ratio exactly.
items.e: Larger samples get closer to the ratio.

items.q: What is natural selection?
c: Organisms with features better suited to the environment survive and reproduce, passing on their alleles.
Organisms change their genes on purpose.
items.e: It leads to evolution.

items.q: What causes Down syndrome?
c: an extra copy of chromosome 21 (47 chromosomes)
items.e: It results from a fault in meiosis.

items.q: What is a gene?

items.e: Genes are found at fixed positions (loci) on chromosomes.

items.q: What is artificial selection?

items.q: What is a mutation?

items.q: Which type of variation is shown by hand span?

items.q: Which is an advantage of selective breeding of rice?

It is faster than genetic engineering for every trait.
Higher yields or resistance to disease can be produced.
It increases genetic variation in the crop.
items.e: It reduces variation, which can be a disadvantage.
